subject: Numeric literals
notes: kb/Work PB1446 landed (w1018d). "The value of a fixed-point numeric literal is the algebraic quantity represented by the characters in the fixed-point numeric literal. The size of a fixed-point numeric literal is equal to the number of digits in the string of characters in the literal." (cite.py --check 8.3.3.3.2 -> OK §8.3.3.3.2 4)). The refuter's one gap (`1 ,5` valued 1.5, the value of characters outside the literal) is closed by the contiguity predicate. VALUE: the COBOL-85 golden pins -,5 = -0.50, +000123,4500 = 123.45, 1,25 * -2 = -2.50, 10 - -1,5 = 11.50 under DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA. SIZE: leading zeros count -- -000000000000000012 (18 digits) is accepted at COBOL-85 and -0000000000000000001 (19 digits, value -1) is refused COBOL0802 at COBOL-85 (negative). The PB1230 constant-entry check: `01 K1 CONSTANT AS 1 ,5.` is refused (COBOL0307), not normalized to 1,5.
